STEP 1 - Scene: A single strip-like cut of cooked bacon (or similar cured pork) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-top-down angle. It looks like a bacon-only serving.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square white dish roughly 22 cm across its width (similar to a side plate). Area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 480 cm² for a square, but the usable well is about 20 cm across, so I use an effective area of ~320 cm² (the plate interior, excluding rim).

STEP 3 - Items: One visible food: cooked bacon, in two connected pieces. The long strip is about 14 cm long and about 2 cm wide, plus a short folded piece about 4 x 3 cm at the left end.

STEP 4 - Area: Long strip ≈ 14 x 2 = 28 cm²; folded piece ≈ 10 cm². Total ≈ 38 cm², about 12% of the plate's effective area.

STEP 5 - Volume: Bacon is thin, about 0.4 cm on average when flattened and curled. Volume ≈ 38 cm² x 0.4 cm ≈ 15 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bacon is dense, bulk density ~0.9 g/ml, giving ≈ 14 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon ≈ 540 kcal/100 g (fat-rich). 14 g x 5.4 ≈ 76 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A couple of cooked bacon strips is typically 15–20 g and about 80–100 kcal, so 14 g and ~75 kcal is plausible for what is visible.

Total: about 14 g, about 76 kcal.
